abstract.t: This document is the PIC Specification: the entry point of the PIC specification set. It defines the normative semantics of the Provenance Identity Continuity (PIC) Model and indexes the subordinate specifications that cover specific domains.

The PIC Specification expresses the execution invariants of the PIC Model in normative form, without redefining, extending, or altering the underlying theoretical model. In case of conflict, the PIC Model publications remain authoritative for the theoretical framework, while this PIC Specification is authoritative for normative requirements and conformance language.

list.t: The PIC Model defines the foundational execution theory and invariants (see ).
The PIC Specification (this document and its subordinate specifications) defines the normative semantics of the PIC Model.

section.name: Requirements Notation
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [2] [3] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

Documents and implementations claiming conformance with PIC MUST faithfully preserve the invariants defined by the PIC Model as expressed by this Specification. Anything that violates these invariants is not PIC-compliant, regardless of naming or intent.
Subordinate specifications:

list.t: MUST NOT redefine, extend, or alter the invariants of the PIC Model,
MUST identify the version of this specification on which they depend,
are canonical only in the version designated by the Specification Steward.

section.name: Core Invariants
section.t: This section is normative.
A PIC-conformant specification, profile, or implementation MUST preserve all of the following invariants:

list.t: A root PIC Context of Authority establishes the upper authority bound for its lineage.
Every accepted non-root advancement MUST continue exactly one causal predecessor.
The selected profile MUST establish the required Proof of Relationship (PoR) relation between the predecessor and successor.
Successor authority MUST be no greater than predecessor authority under the selected profile's attenuation order. For set-valued authority, successor authority is a subset of predecessor authority.
Authority from unrelated lineages MUST NOT be imported into a valid continuation.
A Proof of Continuity is the composition of valid hops that preserve these invariants.

section.t: When a selected profile carries a relational executor envelope or execution contract, the predecessor envelope governs admission of the successor, the successor profile MUST satisfy it under sound evidence, and the carried successor envelope MUST preserve or strengthen it. In logical notation, rho(i+1) => rho(i). Withholding profile evidence MUST NOT widen admission [4].

When a selected profile generalizes carried state to several ordered security coordinates, every ordinary transition MUST be non-expansive in every coordinate under that coordinate's declared semantic order. Any non-conservative coordinate change is an explicit authorized relaxation, not an ordinary continuation [5].

These invariants define full PIC continuity. A concrete profile or implementation MUST NOT claim a Proof of Continuity, the PIC confused-deputy exclusion result, or full PIC conformance merely because it authenticates artifacts, links checkpoint bytes, proves control of a key, or enforces non-expansion. Its receiving predicate MUST also soundly establish the profile's concrete realization of the abstract PoR relation. An implementation that establishes only a strict subset MAY describe those properties as a partial or artifact-linked assurance level, but MUST identify the missing refinement obligations and MUST NOT present that level as full PIC continuity [4].

Claims about concrete protected effects require additional realization obligations: the modeled causal dependencies MUST be complete for the stated threat model, evidence for causal edges MUST be sound, and every protected effect in scope MUST be mediated against the authority state of its occurrence. PIC continuity alone does not prove that hidden state, an omitted physical path, or an unmediated effect was represented [4] [5].

The exactly-one-predecessor rule applies to an ordinary linear advancement. Forks produce separate valid paths. A profile that represents an ordinary multi-parent causal join MUST keep the child security state no more permissive than every parent; for set-valued authority, the child authority is therefore a subset of the intersection of the parent authorities. A composition, grant, endorsement, or other non-conservative transition MUST be explicit and separately authorized and MUST NOT masquerade as an ordinary continuation [5].

section.name: Documents

texttable.c: Normative, implementation-independent requirements for PIC Provers and Verifiers: logical objects, trusted roots, non-root continuity advancements, Proof of Relationship, ordered Verifier checks, authority attenuation, request/execution binding, conformance, and profile-selected representations.

Revocation around stable lineage identifiers, path positions, lineage-depth and causal cutoffs, optional authenticated selectors, position or ancestry witnesses, revocation authorization, and authenticated revocation state.

Sandboxed Execution as an outer ENFORCE PIC continuity governing a Composition Collection of independently verifiable PIC continuities. The collection is bound exactly, members remain independent, and no authority union is created.

Profile-selected PIC deployment architectures, including trusted continuity services, decentralized validation, hybrid enterprise topologies, service meshes, and optional interoperability through selected exchange profiles.
Protocol-neutral same-occurrence binding of PIC authority evidence, IFC evidence, runtime provenance, and other COSS coordinate evidence on one causal history.

section.t: Implementation mappings, product coverage reports, and deployment-specific interoperability notes are maintained outside the normative specification set. They may demonstrate conformance but do not define PIC semantics or modify a profile's requirements.

section.name: Origins, Authorship, and Historical Record
section.t: This section is informative.

The Provenance Identity Continuity (PIC) Model was originally developed by Nicola Gallo as a formal framework for reasoning about causal authority propagation across distributed execution. Its development introduced Proof of Relationship (PoR), Proof of Continuity (PoC), authority non-expansion, relational attenuation, and event-level causal provenance as connected parts of the framework. The PIC Specifications translate those formal results into technical requirements and are published and maintained by Nitro Agility S.r.l. as Specification Steward.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The security consequences of PIC depend on the concrete profile and its realization of PoR, non-expansion, freshness, request or execution binding, revocation, and complete mediation. Authentication of artifacts or possession of keys alone does not establish causal continuity. The subordinate specifications define the detailed security requirements for their respective mechanisms.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: Continuity identifiers, causal relationships, authority contexts, executor evidence, and revocation state can enable correlation across services or execution steps. Profiles and deployments should disclose only the evidence required by the receiving Verifier, scope stable identifiers to the smallest suitable trust domain, and define retention and access controls for continuity records. Data minimization must not remove evidence required for a claimed security property.

section.name: Registry Considerations
section.t: This version defines no shared protocol registry and requests no external registry action. A future wire-format or interoperability profile may define registries for identifiers, algorithms, evidence types, or error values.

section.t: This section is informative.

list.t: 0.2 — 15 July 2026. Initial publication of the 0.2 specification family.

0.2 revision — 26 October 2026. Aligned concrete assurance claims, relational authority, event-level causal provenance, fan-out, and multi-parent composition with the cited formal record; separated the research history from repository licensing and governance; and established the standalone origin, authorship, and historical record used across the specification family. Added the COSS Temporal Evidence subordinate specification for same-occurrence binding of evidence from several security coordinates.
